title: National Consumer Helpline (1915) — pre-litigation grievance redressal
authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
summary: The National Consumer Helpline (1915, consumerhelpline.gov.in) registers consumer grievances, forwards them to companies through the INGRAM system, and issues a docket number — a free first step before approaching consumer commissions.
text:
National Consumer Helpline (NCH) — 1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in (INGRAM portal):

The Department of Consumer Affairs operates the National Consumer Helpline to register consumer grievances against sellers, e-commerce platforms and service providers. A consumer can call 1915 (or register on the portal) and receive a unique docket number; the grievance is forwarded to the company or to the relevant regulator or ombudsman for response.

Many e-commerce and banking disputes resolve at this stage because companies are incentivised to respond to NCH dockets. Registering a grievance also creates a dated record useful later before the consumer commissions.

When it does not work: escalate to a formal complaint on e-Daakhil before the District/State Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, citing the docket and correspondence as evidence of attempted resolution.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — verify current numbers and processes at consumeraffairs.nic.in before relying on it.

title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal & helpline 1930
authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
summary: cybercrime.gov.in is the national portal for reporting cybercrime (including online financial fraud); the helpline 1930 can trigger freezing of defrauded funds. Complaints are routed to state police/cyber cells. Women/child-related cybercrime can be reported anonymously.
text:
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) — cybercrime.gov.in; helpline 1930:

For online financial fraud (UPI scams, phishing, fake apps, unauthorised electronic transactions), speed matters: (1) call the bank's fraud helpline and 1930 immediately — the citizen financial cyber fraud helpline coordinates freezing of remaining funds through the banking system; (2) file a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in (report other cybercrime or women/child-related cybercrime categories; anonymous reporting is allowed for women/child-related complaints); (3) the complaint is routed to the concerned state police cyber cell, which may contact the complainant for statements and documents.

Preserve and attach: transaction IDs (UTR/RRN), account numbers of beneficiary, date-time, device details, chat screenshots, ads/links, and any call recordings.

For follow-up, the local police station or the district cyber cell can be approached with a printed copy of the NCRP complaint and evidence. Compensation for unauthorised electronic transactions also proceeds through bank grievance redressal, the RBI-integrated ombudsman scheme (verify current framework) and consumer commissions.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — verify current processes at cybercrime.gov.in before relying on it.

title: NALSA free legal aid — helpline 15100 and District Legal Services Authorities
authority: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), Supreme Court of India
summary: NALSA's helpline 15100 connects citizens to free legal advice; District Legal Services Authorities at every district court provide panel lawyers, mediation and legal aid to eligible persons under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
text:
NALSA — National Legal Services Authority (nalsa.gov.in, helpline 15100):

Free legal services available: legal advice, drafting support, panel advocates for litigation in courts/tribunals, and mediation through Legal Services Authorities at national (NALSA), state (SLSA) and district (DLSA) levels.

Eligibility (Section 12, Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987) includes women, children, SC/ST members, victims of trafficking, persons with disability, persons in custody, and persons below the income ceiling notified by the state (commonly around ₹3 lakh per annum in several states — verify your state's ceiling).

Lok Adalats: organised periodically by the authorities; awards are deemed civil court decrees and final. Pre-litigation mediation is encouraged for compoundable disputes (cheque cases, minor civil claims, maintenance).

How to reach: call 15100, visit the DLSA office in the district court complex, or use legal aid clinics. Front-line services (Nyaya Bandhu tele-law) also connect citizens with pro bono lawyers.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — verify current details at nalsa.gov.in before relying on it.

title: Labour Commissionerate — wage and employment grievance offices
authority: State Labour Departments / Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India
summary: Assistant Labour Commissioners / Labour Commissioners hear wage-payment grievances, conduct conciliation between employers and workmen, and enforce labour laws including the Payment of Wages Act and Industrial Disputes Act machinery.
text:
Labour department pathway for wage/employment grievances:

Where an employer withholds wages or dues, the employee may approach the office of the Labour Commissioner / Assistant Labour Commissioner (ALC) of the area: (i) officials verify the employment and dues; (ii) conciliation meetings between employer and employee are convened (the Industrial Disputes Act machinery); (iii) where a workman's money is due under a settlement/award/contract, a Section 33C IDA recovery application may be made; (iv) claims under the Payment of Wages Act are entertained by the notified authority.

Related central machinery: EPFO for provident fund dues (epfindia.gov.in), ESIC for employees' state insurance, and the Employees' Compensation Act machinery for workplace injuries. Grievances can also be lodged on the centralised CPGRAMS portal and the labour ministry's Shram Suvidha portal.

Documentation that strengthens the complaint: appointment letter, salary slips, bank statements showing non-payment, employment contract, internal correspondence, and relieving/full-and-final statements.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — office names and procedures vary by state; verify with your state labour department before relying on it.

title: Emergency helplines — 112 (police/emergency), 1091 (women), 1098 (child)
authority: Ministry of Home Affairs / state police, Government of India
summary: 112 is the pan-India emergency number (police, fire, medical). 1091 is the women's helpline, 1098 the child helpline (CHILDLINE), 1930 cybercrime fraud, 15100 legal aid. In situations involving risk to life, violence or unlawful detention, contact emergency services immediately before any documentation work.
text:
Emergency helplines (India):

112 — pan-India emergency response number for police, fire and medical emergencies. In situations involving threats to life, violence, stalking, accidents or unlawful detention, calling 112 is the first step; documentation and legal processes follow.

1091 — women's helpline for harassment, domestic violence and distress; many states also operate 181 as a women & child welfare helpline. One Stop Centres provide medical, police and legal assistance at one place.

1098 — CHILDLINE for children in distress.

1930 — cyber financial fraud helpline (with cybercrime.gov.in for filing).

15100 — NALSA legal aid helpline for free legal advice.

Guidance for urgent legal situations: ensure physical safety first (police/112); preserve evidence without confronting the aggressor; seek medical examination where injured (the medical record becomes evidence); and approach the Protection Officer, Magistrate or High Court through legal aid as appropriate.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — verify current numbers at 112.gov.in and mha.gov.in before relying on them.

title: Civil courts and recovery suits — practical filing note
summary: Money-recovery claims (unpaid deposits, dues, loans) lie before civil courts of competent pecuniary jurisdiction; a legal notice usually precedes the suit; limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963 commonly allows three years for simple contract claims (verify). Court fees vary by state and claim value.
text:
Practical note on civil recovery suits (demo guidance, not legal advice):

Forum: suits for recovery of money are filed before the civil court (or court of small causes / commercial court as applicable) whose pecuniary jurisdiction covers the claim value. Territorial jurisdiction commonly follows residence of defendant or cause of action — verify with local rules.

Pre-suit step: a written demand (legal notice) is customary and, for claims against the government, statutorily required (notice under the applicable state/Central enactment before suing public authorities — verify the notice period for your state).

Limitation: the Limitation Act, 1963 prescribes periods for different claims — commonly three years for simple contract-based recovery from when the breach/cause arises (verify the applicable article and any acknowledgements that reset limitation).

Costs and procedure: court fees are set by state schedules scaled to claim value; pleadings should state facts chronologically with documents exhibited; execution of the decree is a separate stage after judgment.

Alternatives: mediation (including court-annexed and NALSA pre-litigation mediation), arbitration where the contract provides it, and Lok Adalat for compromise-friendly claims.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — a secondary practice note. Verify all limits, fees and procedures with the local court or a lawyer before relying on it.

title: Official portals for verifying Indian legal sources
summary: Primary-authority verification portals: India Code (indiacode.nic.in) for central legislation, eGazette for notifications, Supreme Court and High Court websites for judgments, e-Daakhil for consumer filings, rtionline.gov.in for RTI. Always verify citations against these portals before use.
text:
Official verification portals (India):

India Code (indiacode.nic.in): the official repository of central Acts with amendments — the first stop to verify a section or proviso.

eGazette (egazette.gov.in): government notifications, commencement orders and rules.

Supreme Court of India (sci.gov.in / judgments search) and High Court websites: authoritative text of judgments; SCC and other law reports for reported citations.

e-Daakhil (edaakhil.nic.in): electronic filing and case status for consumer commissions.

rtionline.gov.in: online RTI applications to central public authorities.

cybercrime.gov.in: cybercrime complaints. consumerhelpline.gov.in: consumer dockets. nalsa.gov.in: legal aid. labour.gov.in and state labour department sites: labour machinery.

Why this matters: Nyaya's demo knowledge base is clearly labelled DEMO DATA. Before relying on any cited provision, section number or deadline, verify it on the corresponding official portal above — the knowledge base, not the AI, must remain the source of truth.

DEMO KNOWLEDGE BASE ENTRY — a secondary guidance note.
